name: ESP32

strapping.0: Chip boot mode (with GPIO2). Default weak pull-up (1). GPIO0=1 -> SPI boot; GPIO0=0 and GPIO2=0 -> Joint Download Boot (UART/SDIO download).
strapping.2: Chip boot mode (with GPIO0). Default weak pull-down (0). Must be 0 together with GPIO0=0 to enter Joint Download Boot; ignored when GPIO0=1.
strapping.5: Timing of SDIO slave (with MTDO/GPIO15). Default weak pull-up (1).
strapping.12: MTDI: selects VDD_SDIO (flash/PSRAM supply) voltage at reset. Default weak pull-down (0) -> VDD_SDIO powered from VDD3P3_RTC (typically 3.3 V); 1 -> internal 1.8 V LDO. Overridden if eFuse EFUSE_SDIO_FORCE=1 (then EFUSE_SDIO_TIEH decides). Also JTAG MTDI.
strapping.15: MTDO: U0TXD (ROM boot log) printing control, default weak pull-up (1) = printing enabled, 0 = disabled; also timing of SDIO slave (with GPIO5). Also JTAG MTDO.

psram.condition: Only on chips/modules with PSRAM. Off-package PSRAM (e.g. ESP32-WROVER-E per datasheet): GPIO16 = PSRAM CE#, GPIO17 = PSRAM SCLK (alternatively SD_CLK/GPIO6 may be used for SCLK, freeing GPIO17); PSRAM data lines share SD_DATA_0..3 (GPIO7-10) with flash. In-package PSRAM ESP32-D0WDRH2-V3 (and EOL ESP32-D0WDR2-V3): GPIO16 = CE#, SCLK on SD_CLK (GPIO6). The ESP-IDF GPIO page flags GPIO16-17 as 'SPI0/1 ... usually connected to the SPI flash and PSRAM integrated on the module'.

usb_jtag.note: ESP32 has no USB peripheral (no USB-Serial-JTAG, no USB OTG); none listed in the ESP32 datasheet. Programming/console is via UART0 (usually through an external USB-UART bridge).

adc2_wifi_conflict: ADC2 pins cannot be used when Wi-Fi is used. So, if you are having trouble getting the value from an ADC2 GPIO while using Wi-Fi, you may consider using an ADC1 GPIO instead, which should solve your problem. [GPIO page]  |  ADC2 is also used by Wi-Fi. adc_oneshot_read() has provided protection between the Wi-Fi driver and ADC oneshot mode driver. [ADC oneshot page]
notes: JTAG mapping (datasheet pin overview): MTDI=GPIO12, MTCK=GPIO13, MTMS=GPIO14, MTDO=GPIO15. ESP-IDF GPIO page: 'GPIO12-15 are usually used for inline debug.'
Flash pin mapping (datasheet Table 2-1/2-6): GPIO6=SD_CLK/SPICLK, GPIO7=SD_DATA_0/SPIQ, GPIO8=SD_DATA_1/SPID, GPIO9=SD_DATA_2/SPIHD, GPIO10=SD_DATA_3/SPIWP, GPIO11=SD_CMD/SPICS0.

ESP32-U4WDH (in-package 4 MB flash) uses a DIFFERENT mapping: SD_DATA_1(GPIO8)=IO0, GPIO17=IO1, SD_DATA_0(GPIO7)=IO2, SD_CMD(GPIO11)=IO3, SD_CLK(GPIO6)=CLK, GPIO16=CS#. On that part GPIO16 and GPIO17 are flash pins.

ESP-IDF GPIO page groups GPIO6-11 and GPIO16-17 together as 'SPI0/1: ... usually connected to the SPI flash and PSRAM integrated on the module and therefore should not be used for other purposes.' A conservative audit should treat 16/17 as reserved on any WROVER/PSRAM or U4WDH-based design.

Input-only GPIO34-39 have no output driver and no internal pull-up/pull-down (datasheet Appendix A.1 note 2; ESP-IDF GPIO page 'GPI'). Pin names: SENSOR_VP=GPIO36, SENSOR_CAPP=GPIO37, SENSOR_CAPN=GPIO38, SENSOR_VN=GPIO39, VDET_1=GPIO34, VDET_2=GPIO35.
ESP-IDF GPIO page: 'Please do not use the interrupt of GPIO36 and GPIO39 when using ADC or Wi-Fi and Bluetooth with sleep mode enabled.' (ESP32 errata GPIO-3.11).
Strapping pins are latched at reset; datasheet hold time tH min 1 ms after CHIP_PU goes high. After reset they are usable as normal IO.

GPIO12 (MTDI) strapping high at reset selects a 1.8 V VDD_SDIO; datasheet Table 1-1 lists ESP32-U4WDH and ESP32-D0WDR2-V3 as requiring 3.3 V VDD_SDIO. (Many modules burn EFUSE_SDIO_FORCE; that is module-specific and not asserted here.)
GPIO32/33 double as 32 kHz crystal pins (32K_XP/32K_XN). GPIO25/26 are DAC_1/DAC_2.
ESP-IDF ADC docs (dev-board specific): ESP32-DevKitC GPIO0 cannot be used for ADC oneshot (auto-flash circuit); ESP-WROVER-KIT GPIO0, 2, 4, 15 cannot be used for ADC.
ADC continuous mode on ESP32 uses I2S0 as DMA FIFO (adc_continuous page).
GPIO20 is excluded: neither the ESP-IDF GPIO page (34 GPIOs: 0-19, 21-23, 25-27, 32-39) nor the ESP32 datasheet v5.3 pin overview lists it.

toolchain_prefix confirmed from ESP-IDF docs: xtensa-esp32-elf-gdb (JTAG debugging page) and xtensa-esp32-elf-addr2line (fatal-errors / idf-monitor pages). The installer package itself is named xtensa-esp-elf (idf-tools page); the per-target prefix is what the binaries/commands use.
sources: https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32_datasheet_en.pdf (v5.3: Table 1-1, Table 2-1 Pin Overview, Section 2.3.1, Section 2.6 Tables 2-5/2-6, Section 3 Boot Configurations, Appendix A.1)
